intent.text: An agent is available that turns a brief provided description or intention into a self contained, precise spec. It extracts the provider's tacit knowledge using interview questions. The agent probes the intention's landscape with explorer agents and the provider's tacit knowledge with interview questions; obvious additions are automatic, the focus is questioning the edges, tradeoffs, failure modes and hard parts the provider would not think to volunteer. This agent provides a vital link in the build chain that every other role builds, verifies and reviews from.

scope.text: The agent body at dev/orchestration/crew/spec-interviewer.md and its installed copy at .claude/agents/spec-interviewer.md.
The agent-shaped harness at dev/orchestration/harness/spec-interviewer/ that proves the body, complete to the Pattern B inventory.
The dispatch contracts this agent uses toward explorer, rubric-judge and spec-attacker, as its own inputs and outputs.
The question-bundle and answer-bundle contract through which any interview surface meets this agent.
Revision of a frozen spec into the next version file, and the freeze mechanics performed on the provider's instruction.
Deciding that a spec is ready, or deciding to freeze it: the provider's act.
Attacking or judging its own draft: the rubric-judge and spec-attacker do that from contexts that never saw the interview.
Deriving checks or a tests map from the behaviours it wrote: the test builder's work.
Editing any existing template, schema, validator, linter or convention document; the one new schema this work creates is named in I10.
Writing run conduct into a spec: tools, agent counts, models, budgets, gates, displays.
Reconciling contradictions between other people's documents: the contradiction is reported and the provider decides.
Editing any project code or any file outside the paths the definition of done names; C6 is the boundary of the produced agent at run time, not of this work.
Proposing how the specified thing should be built, or leaning toward a solution.
Writing the kickoff or the plan.
Searching the repository or the web itself: discovery is delegated to explorer agents that return cited answers.
The bodies of the explorer, rubric-judge and spec-attacker agents, and any crew manifest: each is its own work; only their dispatch contracts appear here, and a session uses whichever of them exist.
Any interview rendering surface (page, question tool, chat): a surface is its own work and plugs into the bundle contract of I3 and I4.

constraints.text: node dev/workspace/filebox/validate-spec.mjs <draft> --schema dev/orchestration/schemas/spec.schema.json exits 0 on every draft written.

node dev/orchestration/checks/spec-readiness-lint.mjs <draft> --repo <project root> exits 0 on the draft that any rubric-judge verdict sheet names, with every produced path declared via --deliverable.
A draft contains no reference to the session, the interview, or who said what.

The agent reads only: the intention or draft spec, the spec template and schema, the run log when supplied, explorer returns, judge verdict sheets, attacker findings, and its own files under the run folder.
Every fact about the repository or the world that enters a draft arrives as an explorer return carrying a citation; the agent opens no repository file itself.
The agent writes only under dev/workspace/runs/<spec-name>/ and, on the provider's freeze instruction, the git commit of the frozen spec file.
No bundle asks a question whose answer is stated in the intention, the template, or an explorer return already received.
No question id appears in more than one bundle.
The body carries frontmatter with exactly name, description, tools and model; its paragraphs are single lines; it names no project-specific path.
The body's tools value is Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Agent, AskUserQuestion and its model value is opus; a run may override the model.

The body carries a section headed for each of the nine domains, the spec conventions, the verification addendum rules and the versioning rules, and the agent reads none of those documents at session time.
A bundle carries at most five questions.
No bundle asks the provider to approve the text of a node already written.

interfaces.name: session inputs
interfaces.text: { intention: string | draft_path: path (a spec file whose INT node is the intention), template_path: path, schema_path: path, project_root: path, run_folder: path (dev/workspace/runs/<spec-name>/), run_log_path?: path }.

interfaces.name: draft spec
interfaces.text: dev/workspace/runs/<spec-name>/spec.v<n>.json, shaped by dev/orchestration/templates/spec.template.json; status draft; header reason line carries the owner's name.

interfaces.name: question bundle
interfaces.text: dev/workspace/runs/<spec-name>/interview/bundles/<marker>.json: { marker: string (a problem id from I5), domain: string, problem: string, questions: [ { id: string, text: string, why: string, options: [ { value: string, recommended: boolean } ], allow_comment: true } ], allow_bundle_comment: true, state: open | answered }.

interfaces.name: answer bundle
interfaces.text: Returned by any surface, in chat: a block headed `## <marker>` then per question `### <id>` / `answer: <value | value ...>` or `answer: (unanswered)` / optional `comment: <text>`, then optional `bundle comment: <text>`; several bundles may be returned in one block.

interfaces.name: problem register
interfaces.text: dev/workspace/runs/<spec-name>/interview/problems.json: [ { id: string, kind: string (any hole in the spec; common kinds gap, dual-path, tradeoff, failure-mode, hard-part), domain: string, text: string, state: open | asked | answered | closed, closed_by: { kind: node | return | provider, id: string } | null } ].

interfaces.name: explorer dispatch
interfaces.text: In: { question: string, stage: intent | scope | constraints | interfaces | behaviours | verification, scope_paths?: [path] }. Out: { id: string (X<n>, assigned by the agent at dispatch), answer: string, confidence: certain | probable | guess, pointers: [path], candidates: [ { domain: string, text: string } ] }, at most a screenful. Model tier: small.

interfaces.name: rubric-judge dispatch
interfaces.text: In: { draft_path: path, rubric_path: path }. Out: the rubric's verdict sheet (per question id, yes or no, quotation, reason; per block pass or fail; overall ready to freeze | returned). Model tier: standard.

interfaces.name: spec-attacker dispatch
interfaces.text: In: { draft_path: path, project_root: path } and nothing else. Out: finding lines `finding id · severity · spec ref · description · state` or the literal `no findings`. Model tier: inherit.

interfaces.name: findings ledger
interfaces.text: dev/workspace/runs/<spec-name>/interview/findings.json: [ { id: string, source: judge | attacker, state: asked | absorbed | rejected, ref: { kind: problem | node | reason, value: string } } ].

interfaces.name: handoff
interfaces.text: Final fenced JSON block of the closing message: { draft_path: path, version: integer, counts: { B: integer, E: integer, C: integer }, nodes: { new: [string], changed: [string], retired: [string] }, validator: { exit: integer, errors: [string] }, linter: { exit: integer, failed: [string] }, judge: ready | returned | not run, attacker: no findings | findings: integer | not run, unchecked_names: [ string (a path-shaped name exactly as written in the draft) ], dispatches: [ { agent: string, stage: string, purpose: string } ], statement: string }; schema new at dev/orchestration/schemas/interviewer-handoff.schema.json, generated from this shape.

interfaces.name: harness
interfaces.text: dev/orchestration/harness/spec-interviewer/ with scenarios/, fixture/, rubric.md, calibration/, checks/, run.sh, judge.sh, records/ exactly as the Pattern B inventory states.

behaviours.text: [deterministic] Before any bundle is written, a wave of explorer dispatches with stage intent completes.
[deterministic] Before the first bundle for a domain is written, a wave of explorer dispatches with that domain's stage completes.
[deterministic] The first draft file is written after the intent wave completes and before the first bundle file exists.
[deterministic] Every question belongs to exactly one bundle.
[property] Every question in a bundle names an edge, a tradeoff, a failure mode or a choice between at least two outcomes.
[deterministic] An answer bundle that closes a problem produces the problem's node in the draft in the same turn.
[deterministic] A problem whose bundle returns (unanswered), or which no explorer return closes, becomes a Q node in open_questions carrying the problem id, in the same turn.
[deterministic] A Q node is followed, before any new bundle, by at least one explorer dispatch whose question is the Q text and whose stage is the Q's domain.
[deterministic] Every path-shaped name in the draft is matched by an explorer return with confidence certain and a pointer, or carries the marker (unchecked).

[deterministic] The rubric-judge is dispatched in the turn in which the register holds no problem in state open or asked, open_questions is empty, and the linter exits 0, without a provider message in between.
[deterministic] Each failing judge question is entered in the findings ledger before the judge is dispatched again.

[deterministic] The spec-attacker is dispatched in the turn in which a judge verdict of ready to freeze arrives for the current draft with open_questions still empty, without a provider message in between.
[deterministic] Every attacker finding id appears in the findings ledger with exactly one state.
[deterministic] The status becomes frozen with a commit only after a provider message instructing the freeze and node dev/workspace/filebox/validate-spec.mjs <draft> --for-freeze exiting 0.
[deterministic] Given a frozen version file, new answers or findings produce the next version file per the versioning rules.
[deterministic] A session that receives a run folder with register problems not closed completes an explorer wave scoped to those problems' domains before any new problem is raised.
[property] Every behaviour id in the draft appears in at least one edge's text, or a decision node states that the behaviour has no boundary case and why.
[deterministic] The closing message of a session whose draft the attacker returned `no findings` on ends with the I10 handoff block, validating against its schema.
[deterministic] Across a session, the files created or modified are only those under dev/workspace/runs/<spec-name>/ and, on instruction, the freeze commit.
[deterministic] Across a session, every file read by the agent itself is in the C4 list.
[deterministic] An explorer candidate returned with confidence certain and a pointer is written as a node in its domain in the same turn.
[deterministic] Every problem in the register cites, in its text, an explorer return or a sentence of the intention.
[deterministic] An explorer candidate returned probable or guess becomes a register problem that is asked.
[deterministic] The first draft holds, in every domain, at least one node or the phrase 'empty by decision' with a reason.
[deterministic] Every bundle's marker is the id of a register problem in state asked.
[deterministic] An answer bundle that closes a problem sets that problem's state to closed with closed_by naming the node or the provider, in the same turn.
[deterministic] Every name carrying the marker (unchecked) appears in the handoff's unchecked_names.
[deterministic] Each failing judge question either opens a register problem that is asked, or is absorbed into a named node, before the judge is dispatched again.
[deterministic] A rejected finding carries a reason in its ledger entry.
[deterministic] A frozen version file is byte-identical after any later session.
[deterministic] A session that receives a run folder with register problems not closed re-asks those problems' bundles before any new problem is raised.
[deterministic] A candidate returned probable or guess appears in no node until its problem is answered.
[deterministic] The freeze commit contains only the spec file.

edges.text: The intention describes two pieces of work: the first bundle names both and asks which this spec is, and no other bundle is written until answered (boundary of B3, B4).
A later answer contradicts an earlier node: a dual-path problem is registered and its bundle quotes both and asks which holds; the node is unchanged until answered (boundary of B6, B26, C14).
A supplied draft fails the validator: the errors are listed in the first message, the first write fixes the structure, and the fixes are listed in the handoff (boundary of B3).
The run log is not supplied or unreadable: the session proceeds and the handoff's dispatches list records no run-log question (boundary of B1).
A required input from I1 is missing: the first message asks for it and nothing else; no dispatch is made and no draft is written until supplied (boundary of B1, B3).

An explorer returns probable, guess, or no pointer for a name: the name is written (unchecked), listed in unchecked_names, and a gap problem asks the provider to confirm it or declare it new (boundary of B9, B27).
Two explorer returns contradict each other: a dual-path problem quotes both in one bundle; neither enters a node until answered (boundary of B1, B21, B23, B32).

The provider stops responding: the draft, register and bundles are written as they stand with each unclosed problem as a Q node; no judge or attacker is dispatched and no handoff block is emitted (boundary of B7, B10, B18).
The provider asks the agent to decide: the bundle offers the outcomes with one marked recommended; the problem stays asked until picked (boundary of B5, B6).
The attacker returns `no findings`: no problem is registered; the ledger records the dispatch with no entries and the handoff block is emitted (boundary of B12, B13, B29, B18).

A freeze is instructed while open_questions is non-empty, a register problem is not closed, or the validator fails under --for-freeze: the status is unchanged and the reply lists the blocking ids or errors (boundary of B14, B33).
An edit to a frozen file is requested: the frozen file is unchanged; the edit lands in a new version file per B15 and the reply says so (boundary of B15, B30).

An answer bundle is partial: ids present are recorded; ids absent stay unanswered and their bundle stays open; a block with no recognisable marker is reported and no node changes (boundary of B4, B25, B6, B26).
The run folder does not exist: it is created; a supplied draft whose name field differs from its folder is reported in the first message and the name is written to match the folder (boundary of B3).

The judge returns a verdict sheet that fails its own format (a question without a quotation): the sheet is discarded, the judge is dispatched once more, and a second malformed sheet is registered as a failure-mode problem for the provider (boundary of B10, B11, B28).
A dispatched agent does not return: the dispatch is recorded in the handoff's dispatches list with purpose and no result, and the session continues without it (boundary of B2, B8).

An explorer wave returns nothing certain for a stage: the draft's nodes for that domain are written from the intention alone and a gap problem per unverified claim is registered (boundary of B2, B21, B22, B24).

decisions.text: Project-specific paths, templates and schemas arrive as session inputs; the body embeds none, so one body serves every project.
Discovery is delegated to explorers that return cited answers, never bulk context, because an interviewer that searches for itself dilutes the directives it was given.

The obvious is written unasked and the hard parts are asked, because a provider's time is spent only where tacit knowledge lives; wrong obvious nodes are corrected by answers, the judge and the attacker.
Findings from the judge and the attacker are dispensed by this agent through the ledger, because some findings are false positives and the agent holds the domain knowledge to say so.
Harness-failure handling (hook failures, tool crashes, permission misconfiguration) is deferred to a later version because it belongs to the harness this role runs on, which is still changing.
Running the linter on its own draft is not self-grading: the linter is a fixed script with no judgement.
The role runs as an interactive main session; the human picks its model at launch, so the spec binds no model for it.
Publishing the interview through an artifact skill as a claude.ai link was rejected: it costs tokens and time and fights editing.
The interview is a contract of bundles and a problem register rather than a rendering, so a page, the question tool or plain chat can each serve it without the body changing.
The rubric-judge gates the attacker, because attacks on un-judged drafts returned shape findings and style opinions rather than gaps.
Global assets live under dev/orchestration/ and run assets under dev/workspace/runs/, so a spec's versions, interviews, tests maps and reports sit together.
Explorer waves precede questions and are staged by domain, because the agent has little context and few permissions and cannot know where the gaps are until its explorers have mapped the landscape.
A change to a standard reaches the body by revising this spec and running again, not by the body reading standards at session time.
No provider approval gates the attacker, because the judge's ready verdict is already the gate and a second human step only delayed the attack.
Earlier drafts under dev/workspace/filebox/crew/specs/ are left in place; they are outside this work.

Interview questions and open questions are kept in separate places (bundles and the open_questions array) rather than one list, because a question the register can ask and a hole nobody at the table can plug need different handling: the first waits on the provider, the second waits on an explorer or a later session.
Problem kinds are not a closed list: a kind names whatever hole was found, and the common kinds are suggestions.
B16, B17, B19, B20 and B31 have no boundary case: each is an invariant over the whole session with no varying input, so no edge interrogates them.

verification.text: The product is agent-shaped; checks are built per class from records the harness manufactures. Harness: dev/orchestration/harness/spec-interviewer/ per I11, authored before the body and locked against it. Fixture: fixture/ is a scratch project holding the body installed at fixture/.claude/agents/spec-interviewer.md, a scripted intention, a scripted provider whose answer bundles include one (unanswered), one contradiction of an earlier answer, one request that the agent decide, and one partial bundle; scripted explorer, judge and attacker agents whose returns are fixed per scenario, so no other agent body is required. Run: sh dev/orchestration/harness/spec-interviewer/run.sh writes one record per scenario per repetition into records/; each record holds the transcript, every dispatch prompt and return, and the run folder's files. Deterministic, each a script under checks/ reading records/ and exiting 0 or 1: B1 checks/b01-intent-wave-first.mjs, first explorer dispatch with stage intent completes before the first bundle file exists; B2 checks/b02-wave-per-domain.mjs; B3 checks/b03-draft-before-bundle.mjs; B24 checks/b24-domains-filled.mjs, the first draft file in the record has no empty domain without the phrase and a reason; B4 checks/b04-question-in-one-bundle.mjs, every question id is in exactly one bundle; B25 checks/b25-bundle-markers.mjs, every bundle marker resolves to a register problem in state asked; B6 checks/b06-node-same-turn.mjs; B26 checks/b26-problem-closed-same-turn.mjs, every answered problem is closed with closed_by in the turn of the answer; B7 checks/b07-unclosed-to-q.mjs; B8 checks/b08-explorer-per-q.mjs, at least one dispatch per Q id with matching stage; B9 checks/b09-names-cited.mjs; B27 checks/b27-unchecked-listed.mjs, every (unchecked) marker in the draft has a matching entry in the handoff's unchecked_names; B10 checks/b10-judge-on-clean.mjs; B11 checks/b11-judge-findings-ledger.mjs; B28 checks/b28-judge-findings-resolved.mjs, every ledger entry from the judge has a problem or node ref before the next judge dispatch; B12 checks/b12-attacker-after-ready.mjs; B13 checks/b13-attacker-ledger.mjs; B29 checks/b29-rejected-has-reason.mjs, every rejected ledger entry has a non-empty reason; B14 checks/b14-freeze-on-instruction.mjs; B33 checks/b33-freeze-commit-one-file.mjs, git show --stat of the freeze commit names one file; B15 checks/b15-revision.mjs, a next version file exists after a post-freeze answer; B30 checks/b30-frozen-unchanged.mjs, sha256 of the frozen file unchanged; B16 checks/b16-resume.mjs; B31 checks/b31-resume-reask.mjs, every unclosed problem's bundle file is rewritten with state open before any new problem id appears; B18 checks/b18-handoff-block.mjs validating against dev/orchestration/schemas/interviewer-handoff.schema.json; B19 checks/b19-write-boundary.mjs, git status of the fixture shows only the run folder; B20 checks/b20-read-list.mjs, every Read in the transcript resolves to a C4 path; B21 checks/b21-certain-candidates.mjs, every certain candidate appears as a node in its domain in the turn of its return; B22 checks/b22-problems-cite.mjs, every register problem text names a return id or quotes the intention; B23 checks/b23-uncertain-candidates.mjs, every probable or guess candidate has an asked register problem; B32 checks/b32-uncertain-quarantine.mjs, no probable or guess candidate appears as a node before its problem is answered; C13 checks/c13-body-identical.mjs, cmp of the two files exits 0; C1 and C2 checks/c01-c02-validate-lint.mjs running node dev/workspace/filebox/validate-spec.mjs and node dev/orchestration/checks/spec-readiness-lint.mjs on the produced draft; C3 checks/c03-no-session-refs.mjs; C8 checks/c08-no-repeat-ids.mjs; C9 and C10 checks/c09-c10-body-frontmatter.mjs on the delivered body; C11 checks/c11-standards-encoded.mjs, the body contains the four headed sections and no Read in the transcript resolves to a standards document; C12 checks/c12-bundle-size.mjs; C14 checks/c14-no-approval-questions.mjs, no question text asks for approval of a node id already present in the draft. Property, exit code naming the missing property: B5 checks/b05-questions-dig.mjs, every question has options.length >= 2 or its text contains an edge, tradeoff or failure term from the scenario's term list; B17 checks/b17-edges-cover.mjs; C7 checks/c07-no-obvious.mjs, no question text overlaps a sentence of the intention or an explorer return above the scenario's declared threshold. Statistical: B5 and C7 additionally run N=5 per scenario, holding in at least 4; scenario set declares N and k. Judged, rubric.md derived from B5 and D3 as binary questions, judge in a fresh context reading records/ only, every verdict quoting the transcript lines, calibrated against three records graded by the provider with at least one failure, the first drawn from the verdict sheets recorded in dev/workspace/history/85d743ee_crew-agent-specs-readiness-linting.txt and the rest manufactured by the harness: did each question ask for something the provider would not have volunteered; did the draft written before the first bundle state the obvious correctly for the scripted intention. Edges, one scenario each named in scenarios/: E1 checks/e01-two-ideas.mjs; E2 checks/e02-contradiction.mjs; E3 checks/e03-invalid-draft.mjs; E4 checks/e04-no-run-log.mjs; E5 checks/e05-missing-input.mjs; E6 checks/e06-uncertain-name.mjs; E7 checks/e07-explorers-disagree.mjs; E8 checks/e08-provider-silent.mjs, no judge dispatch and no handoff block in the record; E9 checks/e09-decide-request.mjs; E10 checks/e10-no-findings.mjs; E11 checks/e11-freeze-blocked.mjs; E12 checks/e12-frozen-edit.mjs; E13 checks/e13-partial-bundle.mjs; E14 checks/e14-folder-name.mjs; E15 checks/e15-malformed-sheet.mjs; E16 checks/e16-agent-no-return.mjs; E17 checks/e17-empty-wave.mjs. Control scenario: an intention whose edges are fully stated, where B7 must produce no Q node and B5's judged question must not fire. End-to-end proof: with the body installed in fixture/, the provider plays themselves for one full session on a real intention through to an attacker return of no findings, using whichever explorer, judge and attacker agents exist at the time; the produced draft is handed, alone, to the test builder, which derives a tests map covering every B and E without asking the provider a question. Probe: at the gate the provider, not the builder, chooses one record from records/ and reads it; the record identifier is written to dev/orchestration/harness/spec-interviewer/records/probe.txt. Checks pre-exist and are locked against the body's builder for the duration of the run; sh dev/orchestration/harness/spec-interviewer/judge.sh produces the verdict sheet.

acceptance.text: Every deterministic and property check under dev/orchestration/harness/spec-interviewer/checks/ exits 0 on the records of the run that built the body. Every statistical scenario meets its declared k of N. The judged rubric passes with a calibration record present. The end-to-end proof's tests map covers every B and E with zero provider questions. The paths touched are only dev/orchestration/crew/spec-interviewer.md, .claude/agents/spec-interviewer.md, dev/orchestration/harness/spec-interviewer/, dev/orchestration/schemas/interviewer-handoff.schema.json, and the body and its installed copy are byte-identical. dev/orchestration/harness/spec-interviewer/records/probe.txt exists and names one record identifier present in records/.
